questions.q: What is a Group Policy Object (GPO) before it is linked to anything?
options: Only usable on the domain controller itself
Inert — it has no effect until it's linked to a site, domain, or OU
Automatically applied to every computer in the forest
A replacement for Active Directory
questions.explain: A GPO is just a named collection of settings until it's linked to a site, domain, or OU — linking is what makes it take effect.

questions.q: In what order do GPOs apply, from first to last, under the LSDOU rule?
options: Local, Site, Domain, OU (parent OU before child OU)
All GPOs apply simultaneously with no order
Domain, OU, Local, Site
OU, Domain, Site, Local
questions.explain: LSDOU: Local policy first, then Site, then Domain, then OU — with a parent OU's GPOs applying before a child OU's.

questions.q: A domain-level GPO sets minimum password length to 8. The Finance OU has its own GPO setting it to 14. What happens to Finance users?
options: The two settings average out
Group Policy ignores the second conflicting setting entirely
They need 14-character passwords, because the OU-linked GPO applies after the domain GPO and wins the conflict
They need 8-character passwords, because domain-level settings always win
questions.explain: OU-linked GPOs apply after domain-linked GPOs in LSDOU order, so the closer, later-applied setting wins on a conflict.

questions.q: An OU has Block Inheritance turned on. A GPO linked at the domain level is set to Enforced. Does that GPO still apply to the OU?
options: Only during the next scheduled domain controller reboot
Only if the OU administrator approves it manually
Yes — Enforced overrides Block Inheritance
No — Block Inheritance always wins over Enforced
questions.explain: Enforced (formerly No Override) forces a GPO to apply even to an OU with Block Inheritance turned on.

questions.q: A technician just changed a GPO and wants to confirm it applied to a specific user's machine. What should they do?
options: Edit the GPO a second time to make it apply faster
Run gpupdate /force to refresh immediately, then gpresult /r to confirm which GPOs actually applied
Reinstall Windows on that machine
Wait exactly 24 hours for policy to refresh automatically
questions.explain: gpupdate /force pushes an immediate policy refresh, and gpresult /r shows the Resultant Set of Policy — what actually applied and why.
